newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end higher, secondaries dominate.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end higher, secondaries dominate.

text.p: Share prices closed higher again led by secondary stocks which continued their unabated upward path despite questions of overvaluations.

Blue chips also managed to close in positive territory after a soft opening, helped by some program buying, dealers said. "It's still the second board leading the way," said Chung Tin Fah, research manager at brokerage OSK & Partners. "The market is driven by speculation than anything else."
The Second Board index closed up 7.23 points or 1.28 percent at 574.03, just off its new record high of 574.68 set in intraday trading.
The blue chip-based Composite Index ended 3.56 points higher at 1,113.50, after hitting an early low of 1,108.08.
Dealers said secondary counters continued to be driven by liquidity, provided by punters as well as corporate players and some foreign funds.
"It's difficult to say when the rally will end. It could be next week or even next month," said one institutional dealer.

Chung said the volatility of the local bourse and concern over the interest rates direction here and in the U.S. were keeping most fund managers at the sidelines. For the near term, he expects the Composite Index to move in the 1,100-1,150 range.
